name: Lithuania
tagline: The widest English-taught choice in the Baltics, and free places exist
summary: Lithuania has more English-taught bachelor programmes than Latvia or Estonia and is unusual in that EU citizens can compete for state-funded places on the same terms as Lithuanians. You apply directly to each university rather than through one portal, and Vilnius University alone runs more than 30 bachelor and integrated programmes in English. LSMU in Kaunas is the medical draw, and it exempts IB students with HL 5 in the required subjects from its entrance exam.
whyConsider: Vilnius University runs 30+ English-taught bachelor and integrated programmes - unusually deep for a country this size
EU citizens can apply for state-funded places, not just fee-paying ones
LSMU's English-taught Medicine, Dentistry and Veterinary Medicine are open and well-established
IB HL 5 in the required subjects exempts you from LSMU's entrance examination
Tuition starts at around EUR 1,300 a year for some bachelor programmes
watchOuts: No central admissions portal for international students - each university sets its own deadlines and fees
Deadlines are late by Nordic standards (most autumn deadlines are in June or July), which is fine for IB results in July but leaves little planning time
Your secondary qualification must be recognised, and document recognition 'may take up to one month or longer'
Medicine at LSMU is not cheap: EUR 12,800 a year for years 1-3 in 2026/2027, plus a EUR 150 application fee, a EUR 250 registration fee and a EUR 1,500 deposit
The competitive-score formula used for state-funded places was not published in English on the pages read - ask the university how your IB grades will be scored

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Set per programme. LSMU requires Biology and Chemistry on the transcript for its medical programmes (Mathematics and Biology for Health Psychology), and states that International Baccalaureate holders with '5 (H level)' in the required subjects are exempt from its entrance examination.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: Your secondary qualification must be certified/recognised by the Centre for Quality Assessment in Higher Education (SKVC) before a Lithuanian university can admit you. No public IB-to-Lithuanian ten-point conversion table was found on the pages read on 2026-09-22.
notes: Vilnius University explicitly lists the International Baccalaureate among the qualifying education systems it accepts.
ISM accepts an International or European Baccalaureate diploma as proof of English on its own, without a separate language test.

Study in Lithuania states applicants need 'a diploma of secondary education (school leaving certificate or corresponding document from your country certified by the Centre for Quality Assessment in Higher Education)'.
Recognition can take a month or more, so start it as soon as you have your Diploma in July.
Non-EU/non-EFTA applicants to Vilnius University must present a qualification no more than 5 years old; this does not affect a 2027 IB graduate.

portal.name: Study in Lithuania (national information portal; applications go direct to each university)

deadlines.label: LSMU - application portal opens
deadlines.notes: Published for the 2026 intake as "1 November 2025 - Opening the online application period. All applicants must apply at apply.lsmuni.lt and upload copies of all required documents." LSMU publishes a dated "Application calendar" for one intake at a time; on 23 September 2026 it still showed the 2026 intake, headed "RULES FOR ADMITTING STUDENTS TO THE LITHUANIAN UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES IN 2026". The date here is that calendar rolled forward by one year and is provisional until LSMU publishes the 2027 one. Review of applications begins nine days later, on 10 November, and LSMU says plainly what that means: "Applicants are recommended to apply as early as possible. Applications submitted after the deadline could be considered only in case of available study places." An early application also buys you a choice of entrance-test date, which a late one does not.

deadlines.label: Get your IB Diploma recognised - no deadline, and it is the step that runs out of time
deadlines.notes: Nobody publishes a date for this, which is why it needs one of your own. The national portal warns: "Document recognition and subject equivalence identification procedures may take up to one month or longer." Lithuanian universities either recognise the qualification themselves as part of admission - LSMU does, "following the Procedure for Academic Recognition of Foreign Qualifications" - or send you to SKVC, the Centre for Quality Assessment in Higher Education, first. Which of the two applies is set by the university, so ask before you assume. SKVC’s own site (skvc.lt) returned HTTP 500 to every automated request on 23 September 2026 and was also blank when opened in a browser, so its published processing time and any fee could not be recorded here and should not be assumed. Set your own date: start recognition at least two months before the university deadline you are aiming at.

deadlines.label: LSMU - entrance tests and motivational interviews begin
deadlines.notes: Published for the 2026 intake as "13 January 2026 - The period of Entrance tests and motivational interviews starts." LSMU publishes a dated "Application calendar" for one intake at a time; on 23 September 2026 it still showed the 2026 intake, headed "RULES FOR ADMITTING STUDENTS TO THE LITHUANIAN UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES IN 2026". The date here is that calendar rolled forward by one year and is provisional until LSMU publishes the 2027 one. The test is online: an interview a few days before a 90-minute multiple-choice paper in Biology and Chemistry, 30 questions each (Biology and Mathematics for Psychology). Missing the interview cancels the written test automatically, and a date can only be changed with an admission officer’s approval. IB holders with grade 5 at higher level in the required subjects are exempt from the entrance examination altogether, which is the single biggest reason for an IB candidate to look at LSMU. Without a TOEFL, IELTS or CEFR B1 certificate you must also sit LSMU’s own English test.

deadlines.label: ISM University - early admission closes
deadlines.notes: ISM runs four rounds and publishes the whole ladder for one year at a time; on 23 September 2026 it still showed 2026, so this is that calendar rolled forward. Early admission runs "November 1 - April 30", with the online test in the first week of May, the study contract signed by 20 May and the advance payment made no later than 31 May. Worth noting that ISM’s own page carries two stale years inside the 2026 calendar - the early round says "must be submitted by the deadline: April 30th, 2025" under a step headed 30 April 2026, and the additional round says "15th of August, 2025" under a step headed 14 August 2026 - so read the step headings rather than the sentences beneath them, and confirm anything you are relying on.

deadlines.label: Vilnius University - applications close for EU/EFTA citizens
deadlines.notes: Vilnius University was missing from this calendar entirely, although it is the university this profile sends you to first. It has one intake a year and splits the deadline by citizenship. For autumn 2026 the page read: "1 May for applicants from non-EU/EFTA countries" and "1 July for applicants who are citizens of EU/EFTA countries and for non-EU/EFTA applicants with a 90-day visa-free period that has not yet been exceeded". A Danish citizen is in the July group. The 2027 dates were not published on 23 September 2026 - admissions.vu.lt offered only a "Get 2027 Admissions Updates" sign-up - so no date is recorded here. Two things that are not dates but behave like them: the application fee is 100 EUR, non-refundable, and "An online application will be processed only after the application fee is collected and the application is submitted with all the required documents", so an unpaid invoice on the closing day is a missed deadline; and admission can close early, because the published deadline runs only until the limit of study places is reached. EU and EFTA citizens may apply for state-funded as well as fee-paying places. The dates on this page are rendered by JavaScript and are invisible to a plain fetch - they had to be read in a browser on 23 September 2026.

deadlines.label: LSMU - primary application deadline, and it closes at midnight the night before
deadlines.notes: The trap is the time, not the date. LSMU publishes "6 July 2026 - Application deadline. The online application system will be closed on 6 July at 00:00", which means the system is already shut when 6 July begins - the last day you can actually submit is 5 July. LSMU publishes a dated "Application calendar" for one intake at a time; on 23 September 2026 it still showed the 2026 intake, headed "RULES FOR ADMITTING STUDENTS TO THE LITHUANIAN UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES IN 2026". The date here is that calendar rolled forward by one year and is provisional until LSMU publishes the 2027 one. It falls in the same week as IB results, so assemble and submit the application before results day rather than after it. An additional admission round for selected programmes opens the following day, 7 July.

deadlines.label: ISM University - main admission closes for visa-free countries
deadlines.audience: citizens of visa-free countries, which includes Denmark
deadlines.notes: This is the ISM deadline that actually applies to a Danish applicant, and it was buried in a note on the April round. ISM runs main admission twice, on different dates for different passports: "Main admission. For candidates from visa regime countries (May 1 - May 31)", closing 31 May with the contract signed by 12 June, and "Main admission. For candidates from visa - free regime and CIS countries (May 1 - July 24)", closing 24 July with the contract signed by 31 July. An EU citizen is in the second group and has nearly two more months than the first. Rolled forward from the 2026 calendar, which was still the one published on 23 September 2026.

deadlines.label: LSMU - final application deadline
deadlines.notes: The second and last LSMU deadline, with the same midnight trap as the first: "30 July 2026 - Application deadline. The online application system will be closed on 30 July at 00:00." LSMU publishes a dated "Application calendar" for one intake at a time; on 23 September 2026 it still showed the 2026 intake, headed "RULES FOR ADMITTING STUDENTS TO THE LITHUANIAN UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES IN 2026". The date here is that calendar rolled forward by one year and is provisional until LSMU publishes the 2027 one. The last published entrance test sits on the same calendar day at 10:00, after the application system has already closed, so the test is for people who applied earlier - this is not a date on which anything can still be started. After it: the 150 EUR application fee and the 250 EUR registration fee are invoiced with their own deadlines, and LSMU says twice that "Failure to pay the fee on time will result in stopping your admission procedure", as does failing to sign the study contract by the date in the Dean’s letter.

deadlines.label: ISM University - submit your final IB Diploma
deadlines.year: 2027 entry, inferred from an undated annual rule
deadlines.notes: Promoted because it applies to every ISM round and appears in none of their headings: each of the four admission rounds lists "Copy of Final diploma of Secondary Education submitted by the 1st of August". You can be admitted on predicted grades months earlier and still lose the place here. Your IB Diploma is issued in early July, so the gap is about four weeks. Rolled forward from the 2026 calendar.

deadlines.label: ISM University - additional admission round, visa-free countries only
deadlines.audience: citizens of visa-free countries, which includes Denmark
deadlines.notes: A genuine second chance, and one only an EU or other visa-free applicant gets: "Additional admission. Only for candidates from visa - free regime and CIS countries (July 22 - August 14)", with the study contract signed by 18 August and studies starting in early September. Note that ISM’s own page contradicts itself here - the step heading says 14 August 2026 and the sentence under it says "15th of August, 2025" - so work to the earlier of the two and confirm with the admissions office. Rolled forward from the 2026 calendar.

deadlines.label: LSMU - studies begin
deadlines.notes: Published for the 2026 intake as studies beginning at the start of September, with "Student Registration Week takes place a week before" - so the week of late August is not optional and not a holiday. LSMU publishes a dated "Application calendar" for one intake at a time; on 23 September 2026 it still showed the 2026 intake, headed "RULES FOR ADMITTING STUDENTS TO THE LITHUANIAN UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES IN 2026". The date here is that calendar rolled forward by one year and is provisional until LSMU publishes the 2027 one. Before you travel there is the 1,500 EUR deposit for EU/EEA students to pay on top of the application and registration fees.

deadlines.label: Everything else - each university sets its own date
deadlines.notes: There is no national application and no national deadline for international students in Lithuania, so beyond the three universities dated in this calendar you have to ask each institution. The national portal publishes only a pattern: "The deadlines to apply for the autumn semester at most universities are in June, however, international students are strongly advised to apply as early as possible", followed by the warning that recognition can take a month or more. Read on 23 September 2026 without a year attached, which is why no date is recorded. Note how far the three dated universities sit from that June pattern - LSMU closes in July, ISM in late July for an EU applicant, Vilnius on 1 July - so "most universities close in June" is a reason to check, not a date to plan around.

steps: Choose the university and programme first - there is no single national application for international students and each institution runs its own process and its own deadline.

Check how your IB Diploma gets recognised. Some universities do it inside admission (LSMU does), others send you to SKVC first. Either way it can take a month or more, so start it two months before the deadline you are aiming at.

Check which deadline is yours. ISM and Vilnius both publish different closing dates for visa-free and visa-required applicants, and as a Danish citizen you get the later one - 24 July at ISM, 1 July at Vilnius - but only if you read the right line.

Apply on the university’s own portal with your transcript, passport, proof of English and, at Vilnius University, a motivation letter of 1,200-4,000 characters. Vilnius University charges EUR 100 per application, which covers up to three programme choices, and will not process the application until the fee has cleared.

Sit any required assessment. LSMU runs an interview plus a 90-minute multiple-choice examination in Biology and Chemistry, but exempts IB candidates with HL 5 in those subjects. ISM requires a state mathematics examination result or its own mathematics test.

Pay the fees that fall due on acceptance: at LSMU that is a EUR 150 application fee, a EUR 250 registration fee and a EUR 1,500 deposit for EU/EEA students. Missing any of those invoice dates stops the admission.
Send your final IB Diploma the week it arrives - ISM wants it by 1 August whichever round admitted you.
As an EU citizen, move to Lithuania and complete the residence registration; non-EU students arrange a national visa and residence permit before travelling.
application.selectionNotes: Selection is per programme and, for state-funded places, competitive. Vilnius University confirms that citizens of Lithuania and of other EU member states 'can apply for both state-funded and non-state-funded study places' - this is a genuine advantage over Latvia. The exact competitive-score formula, and how IB grades are weighted inside it, was not published in English on the pages read on 2026-09-22.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Extensive by Baltic standards. Vilnius University alone offers more than 30 bachelor's and integrated study programmes in English; ISM offers six; LSMU offers Medicine, Dentistry, Veterinary Medicine, Pharmacy, Nursing, Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy, Dental Hygiene and Health Psychology in English. A national total was not published on the pages read.
language.englishProof: Varies by university. ISM accepts an International or European Baccalaureate diploma in place of a language test, and otherwise requires its own English test (55), TOEFL iBT 60, IELTS 6.0, Cambridge B2 169, PTE Academic 52 or Duolingo 115. LSMU states a requirement of IELTS above 5.5 or CEFR B1 or equivalent (its page also lists a TOEFL figure that reads as a typographical error - confirm directly). Vilnius University requires proof of language proficiency from its own approved list.
notes: English-taught programmes are taught fully in English; Lithuanian is not required for the degree.
Clinical placements in medicine involve Lithuanian-speaking patients, so medical students normally take Lithuanian language courses alongside the degree - check how your programme handles this.

tuitionEuEea.value: State-funded places are open to EU citizens and cost nothing. Fee-paying places start 'from 1.300 EUR per year for Bachelor studies' as a national average across institutions, rising steeply for medicine. LSMU does not distinguish EU from non-EU tuition rates.
tuitionEuEea.year: Study in Lithuania figure undated on the page read on 2026-09-22

tuitionNonEu.value: LSMU 2026/2027, same rates for EU and non-EU: Medicine EUR 12,800 (years 1-3) and EUR 13,300 (years 4-6); Odontology EUR 13,600 (years 1-3) and EUR 14,100 (years 4-5); Veterinary Medicine EUR 9,200 (years 1-3) and EUR 10,700 (years 4-6); Pharmacy EUR 5,600 (years 1-3) and EUR 5,700 (years 4-5); Nursing EUR 4,300 a year; Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy, Dental Hygiene and Health Psychology EUR 4,201 a year.

costs.applicationFee: Vilnius University EUR 100 per application, non-refundable, covering up to three programme choices. ISM EUR 100. LSMU EUR 150 application fee plus a EUR 250 registration fee and a EUR 1,500 deposit for EU/EEA students.
notes: Monthly living costs in Vilnius or Kaunas were not published on any official page read on 2026-09-22 - this figure needs checking before it is used on the site.
Fees at LSMU step up in the clinical years, so budget for the higher figure from year 4.

funding: State-funded ('budget') study places are open to EU citizens on the same terms as Lithuanians. This is the single most valuable form of funding available and is worth investigating before you look at scholarships.
Individual universities run their own merit scholarships; details were not verified on the pages read.
Danish SU for a full degree abroad requires approval of the programme by Uddannelses- og Forskningsstyrelsen - confirm with your studievejleder.
residency: As a Danish or other EU citizen you have the right to live and study in Lithuania and complete a residence registration for stays over three months. Non-EU students need a national visa and a temporary residence permit arranged before travelling; Vilnius University keeps a dedicated page on visas and residence permits. The precise EU registration procedure was not confirmed on the pages read on 2026-09-22.
housing: Universities run dormitories and international offices normally help arrange a room once you accept a place. Rents in Vilnius and Kaunas are well below Nordic levels. Specific dormitory application deadlines were not published on the pages read.
healthcare: As an EU citizen bring your EU health insurance card for necessary care. Non-EU students must arrange health insurance as part of the residence permit application. Detailed requirements were not published on the pages read.

institutions.name: Vilnius University
institutions.englishBachelors: More than 30 bachelor's and integrated study programmes in English
institutions.note: One of the oldest universities in Northern Europe, with by far the widest English-taught choice in the Baltics and state-funded places open to EU citizens.

institutions.name: Kaunas University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Part of a catalogue of more than 120 study programmes; the English-taught bachelor count was not published on the pages read
institutions.note: The main technical university, strongly tied to industry, and the obvious choice if you want engineering rather than medicine or business.

institutions.name: Lithuanian University of Health Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: Medicine, Odontology, Veterinary Medicine, Pharmacy, Nursing, Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy, Dental Hygiene and Health Psychology in English
institutions.note: The Baltic medical school most used to international applicants - and it exempts IB students with HL 5 in Biology and Chemistry from its entrance examination.

institutions.name: ISM University of Management and Economics
institutions.englishBachelors: Six: Business Management and Marketing; Economics and Politics; Economics and Data Analytics; Entrepreneurship and Innovation; International Business and Communication; Finance
institutions.note: Small private business school that accepts an IB diploma as English proof on its own, and runs an early admission round in April.

institutions.name: Vytautas Magnus University
institutions.englishBachelors: Several across social sciences, humanities and IT; count not verified
institutions.note: The most liberal-arts-like university in Lithuania - you take a minor alongside your major, which suits IB students used to breadth.

institutions.name: Vilnius Gediminas Technical University
institutions.englishBachelors: Several in engineering, architecture, aviation and business; count not verified
institutions.note: Strong in civil engineering and aeronautics, including an aviation engineering programme you will not find elsewhere in the region.

institutions.name: Mykolas Romeris University
institutions.englishBachelors: Several in law, business and public governance; count not verified
institutions.note: Social sciences and law focused, with English-taught law programmes that are rare in continental Europe.

institutions.name: Klaipeda University
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number, mainly marine and environmental; count not verified
institutions.note: Lithuania's only coastal university and the place for marine science; small, and outside the capital.

institutions.name: LCC International University
institutions.englishBachelors: All bachelor programmes taught in English
institutions.note: An American-style liberal arts college on the Baltic coast where everything is taught in English and classes are very small.

institutions.name: Vilnius Academy of Arts
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor teaching is mainly in Lithuanian; English-taught bachelor options not verified
institutions.note: The national art academy, with campuses in four cities; entry is portfolio-based and you should assume Lithuanian at bachelor level unless told otherwise.

institutions.name: Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre
institutions.englishBachelors: Bachelor teaching is mainly in Lithuanian; English-taught bachelor options not verified
institutions.note: The national conservatoire and drama school; entry is by audition. Checked 2026-09-23: LMTA has rebuilt its site in Lithuanian only. The English pages were not carried across and now live on old.lmta.lt, which is where the admissions link points; it is short, and the substantial guidance for applicants is on the Lithuanian side.

institutions.name: Kaunas University of Applied Sciences
institutions.englishBachelors: A small number of professional bachelor programmes in English; count not verified
institutions.note: Applied and vocational rather than academic - professional bachelor degrees with placements, and lower entry requirements than the universities.
